svg.desc: M1 in progress · committed source baseline. Reading order follows the normal fluent launch. Every failure follows the cleanup boundary applicable to the resources already acquired. Direct low-level use retains its explicit contracts.

a.title: Ordinary scene construction retains an owning description; managed controls are created lazily. Before preparation configure is queued; after preparation admitted configure runs immediately. Admission guards still apply. ui::launch can avoid evaluating the scene factory for CLI help.

Preparation validates options, creates Application then ManagedScene, installs the observer and applies the theme. It has not opened the native terminal. Explicit prepareChecked permits this boundary before run.

The recipe mounts retained nodes and bindings. Deferred configure callbacks run in registration order after successful mount; the first latched failure stops later configuration. Rejected short setup mutations retain their typed cause, including inside a void configure. Cleanup releases partial resources; external callback effects are not rolled back.

Native transport opens after preparation; a caller-provided transport is borrowed synchronously. Application run is single-use and checks thread affinity. Input, Scheduler, router and frames use the same runtime. Native open failure also requires explicit managed cleanup.

On exit or failure the runner requests stop, stops Scheduler and calls scene.stop. ui::onStop releases external services borrowing Application before managed teardown. Callback failure is captured and terminal close is still attempted. Cancellation is not a hard shutdown deadline.

Terminal close attempts restoration. The fluent boundary then revokes public observation, clears live controllers, closes ManagedScene and retires recipe/configuration captures. Original failure, independent application/restoration detail and cleanup failure remain distinguishable.

Scene::run returns typed expected. runApp reports only after its run and cleanup boundary, returning 0 for success or 1 for failure. Its default final sink writes stderr; a custom sink controls presentation. Factory/setup wrappers cover work inside their callables, not argument evaluation before entry.
